# Did You Ask a Good Question? A Cross-Domain Question Intention Classification Benchmark for Text-to-SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#triagesql)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.12634v1) · arXiv:2010.12634v1, 23 October 2020

**Reading coverage:** All substantive text on PDF pages 1-5, Tables 1-5 and figure descriptions; remaining pages contain references, with no appendices.

## Research question

A text-to-SQL interface must distinguish queries it should translate from unrelated, underspecified or unsupported inputs.

## Method

TriageSQL combines existing SQL, question-answering and table-to-text corpora into five intention classes: answerable, improper, missing external knowledge, ambiguous and outside common SQL grammar. Schema ablation creates missing-knowledge cases; removing irrelevant columns also creates answerable controls.

## Evaluation

Schemas are disjoint across splits. SQL-knowledgeable annotators select and check 2,500 balanced test examples. A RoBERTa-base classifier receives question and serialized schema; training is capped at 10,000 examples per class.

## What the results support

Macro F1 is 0.60, with ambiguous-question F1 0.17 and confusion between answerable and missing-knowledge cases. Irrelevant-column-removal controls materially increase difficulty.

## Limits and qualifications

Most training examples are transformed from heterogeneous corpora, and the paper identifies train/test mismatch and naturally occurring questions as future work. Non-SQL includes limitations of then-common parser grammar, not only logically impossible SQL questions. No generated SQL or recovery dialogue is evaluated.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A foundational input-triage benchmark whose labels should not be treated as timeless proofs of unanswerability.
